chapter: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
title: Jap Allen vs. McKinney's Cotton Pickers battle of bands
summary: Booker and Ben join Jap Allen, and McKinney's men accuse Allen of stealing arrangements Clyde Hart transcribed from records.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving

blocks.x: And of course this is the time that Ben Webster is with Jap Allen, and Basie and all of 'em is in the Eblon Theater, and we drinking this beer, and this meddled whiskey together, and hanging out all together, and all the musicians -- Booker Pittman is blowing the bell out of the saxaphone by this time. And now he's working with Basie on 12th Street with a little four-piece group, and he's blowing everybody out that coming near in there.

Ben Webster is blowing all kind of tenor saxophone now, and he -- with Jap Allen, Clyde Hart tried hard -- is sitting by the record player putting nickles in it and writing all of McKinney's Cotton and music players, copping solos and everything, and making arrangements for Jap Allen. By this time Booker Pittman and Ben Webster had joined Jap Allen, and finally they played a battle of music with McKenny's Cottonpickers at
15 Paseo Hall. [Paseo Hall - on 15th at Paseo]

And McKenny's Cottonpickers had been traveling through the east, and their repertory had been stolen, and when they heard Jap Allen from the arrangements that Clyde had they went and called the police, because they thought they had their music, but Clyde had actually copied it off the record, transcribed their music and Jap Allen's band was playing this music.
He thought they'd stolen the book there.

They thought they had stole the book. Don Edmund was with the band at that time, and they were really something else, you know. They had just about one of the best dance bands in the country at that time.
And they thought that Jap Allen had stole the music, and they find that Clyde Hart had transcribed all these music off the records. Brilliant musician.
